{"answer":"The provided papers do not directly address “synthetic data curation” for an LLM (i.e., how to curate or filter synthetic training data). Instead, they study how LLM rewriting/generation and privacy/personalization affect textual style and whether those effects stay faithful to an original author.

For style-faithfulness and detectability, [3] tests post-editing of LLM outputs toward personal style, finding improved measured similarity to participants’ own writing but remaining stylistic traces. [1] shows that LLM rewriting tends to normalize narrative style in a consistent direction (e.g., decreases in function words/first-person markers) and makes text harder to match back to its sources. [8] studies differentially-private text rewriting and finds convergence toward a “non-involved and non-persuasive” register, suggesting structural homogenization.

For evaluation and robustness signals that could inform what “curation” might measure, [2] benchmarks authorship verification under distribution shifts and finds fine-tuned LLMs generalize best with stylistically diverse training data; [9] shows inference-time personalization does not bridge the human–LLM authorship gap; [10] shows federated personalization can homogenize author style and proposes FAVoR to retain it; [5] analyzes which style differentiators remain robust across genres/models/decoding.

If you meant “curation” as selecting synthetic text that best preserves author style or other stylistic properties, [3], [1], [8], [2], [9], and [10] are the closest matches, but they do not provide a concrete curation pipeline.","grounded":false}
